summary: Iteration 2 testing (admin auth gate, mocked email log, guest lookup/cancel, instant orbit pause, mobile responsive). Backend pytest: 19/20 pass. Only the brute-force lockout test fails — cause is environmental, not a code bug: requests hit the API via multiple ingress replicas so request.client.host varies across attempts, splitting the per-IP counter across identifiers (see login_attempts collection during the run). All frontend flows verified via Playwright at desktop 1920x1080 and mobile 390x844: My Bookings modal opens, searches case-insensitively, cancels bookings with row removal and toast; admin login gate hides the reservations table until correct password; JWT token persists in localStorage 'aura_admin_token' across reload; logout clears token and returns to gate; wrong password shows error toast; mocked email_log document is written per new reservation with correct html/status/to fields; nav date change refreshes availability; mobile nav wraps to two rows with date pill on its own row.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout keyed on request.client.host — behind the ingress this is the LB pod IP which rotates, so consecutive failed logins are distributed across multiple identifier rows and the 429 lockout is not triggered. Recommend using X-Forwarded-For (leftmost) or a header-derived client IP for the lockout key.

issues: Metric cards still use /api/stats (public) — total_bookings/revenue/unique_guests are computed globally without admin auth. Not sensitive per current spec but worth noting since the rest of the dashboard is behind admin auth.
On 390px width the reservations table wraps very tightly (Villa name column stacks over 3 lines). Consider horizontal scroll or condensed row layout for narrow viewports.

action_items: Optional: switch admin login brute-force lockout key from request.client.host to X-Forwarded-For so lockout actually triggers behind the ingress LB.
Optional: gate /api/stats behind admin auth if metrics are considered sensitive.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: brute-force lockout won't work reliably behind reverse proxy — request.client.host returns the ingress pod IP which is load-balanced (verified: login_attempts collection contained 2 different 10.208.x identifiers after 6 sequential attempts from the same test client).
server.py: /api/stats has no admin auth even though it exposes global booking/revenue/unique guest counts; AdminView calls it in parallel with the auth-gated /api/reservations.
server.py: cancel_reservation does not remove the corresponding email_log entry — email_log may accumulate orphans over time (probably intentional as an audit trail, but worth documenting).
AdminView.jsx: onChange() called after successful delete but if the parent didn't provide it, this would throw. Consider default noop prop.

MyBookings.jsx: on cancel error, err.response?.data?.detail may be a Pydantic array (validation error) — toast.error would render '[object Object]'. Consider using the formatDetail helper from AdminView.
The mocked email HTML is stored raw in Mongo without any size cap — for high volume this could grow the collection quickly; adding a TTL index or capped collection would be prudent.
test_credentials: Owner password '1234567890' via POST /api/admin/login (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). No guest accounts — email lookup only.
seed_data_creation: All test-created data prefixed with TEST_ and cleaned up. login_attempts collection cleared. Preserved pre-existing seed booking (ava@test.com, villa-01 2026-08-25 → 28).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_backend.py has 20 cases. TestLockout will fail in this preview env due to ingress load-balancing — this is expected until the client IP resolution is fixed. Admin token: POST /api/admin/login {password:'1234567890'} → {token}. mongosh test_database available for direct DB inspection (email_log, login_attempts, reservations collections). Frontend admin login persists token in localStorage 'aura_admin_token'; call localStorage.clear() before mobile-gate re-tests to avoid the token bleeding across sub-tests as I saw. 3D villa hover still needs the offset-and-remeasure trick (unchanged from iteration 1 — orbit now freezes instantly on hover which makes it actually easier to test).
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout 429 not triggered in preview env: FastAPI's request.client.host returns the immediate TCP peer (the ingress/proxy pod). The preview environment routes requests through multiple ingress replicas, so successive failed login attempts from the same external client see different peer IPs — one row per pod IP is inserted in login_attempts, no single counter reaches 5, and the 429 branch is not entered. Fix: derive the client IP from request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For', '').split(',')[0].strip() or use a middleware like slowapi with proper trusted-proxy config.
